newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-GOALKEEPER CALLS FANS "ANIMALS" AFTER ATTACK.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GOALKEEPER CALLS FANS "ANIMALS" AFTER ATTACK.

text.p: A goalkeeper suffered concussion and needed stitches after being beaten up by fans who invaded the pitch at the end of a Brazilian championship match on Sunday.
Ricardo Pinto, goalkeeper of championship leaders Atletico Paranaense, was attacked during a huge brawl at the end of his team's 3-2 win away to Fluminense in Rio de Janeiro.
Pinto had to leave Fluminense's Laranjeiras stadium in a police car but before he departed, he branded Fluminense's fans as "animals".

Fluminense fans were incensed to see Pinto, who spent nine years at Fluminense earlier in his career, vigorously celebrating a win that made Atletico the first team to be guaranteed a place in the quarter-finals of the competition.
Fluminense fans, who saw their own team slump into last place in the table, had insulted Pinto before the game and thrown objects at him during it.

When the final whistle went, dozens of fans jumped over the fences arond the pitch and a group attacked Pinto, who attempted to retaliate and was struck again. Pinto was eventually saved by members of the Atletico staff who dragged him into the changing rooms.
Police with truncheons came onto the field but there appeared to be too few of them to stop the trouble.

There had been trouble two minutes before the end of the game when Fluminense goalkeeper Leo joined his team's attack, then rushed across the penalty area and lunged into Pinto. The referee took no action.
Leo was also involved in a brawl with Atletico staff at the end and claimed later that he had been insulted by them during the match.

"I celebrated the fact that we had qualified. I celebrated just as I did when we won at home and when we won at Internacional," Pinto said, with a huge bandage around his head. "But in those places, they didn't have animals. Unfortunately, here I found animals."
Other Atletico players huddled in a corner of the stadium and had to wait an hour before they could leave. As their coach pulled out, it was pelted with stones.

Last week, another game in Rio was interrupted for 20 minutes when Vasco directors invaded the pitch to protest a refereeing decision. Vasco eventually won the game 2-1 against Botafogo, but when they scored the winner, Botafogo directors also invaded the pitch to protest.
In the 1966 World Cup tournament, England coach Sir Alf Ramsey caused outrage in Argentina when he labelled members of the country's national team as animals following a tumultuous quarter-final tie.
